paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus cares more about the person in front of Him than about the rule the leader wanted to hide behind. A woman had been bent over for eighteen years, and Jesus saw her, called her over and set her free (Luke 13:11-13). The synagogue leader was indignant, and I think he had so much calendar in his head that he had no room left for her (Luke 13:14).

Now look at how Jesus answers him. He points out that every one of them unties his ox or donkey on the Sabbath and leads it to water (Luke 13:15). Then He calls her a "daughter of Abraham" and says Satan had kept her bound for eighteen long years (Luke 13:16). She was never an interruption to the day. In that synagogue, she was exactly who the day was for.

So what does that mean for you, baker? Check your own heart for the places where you'd rather be tidy than kind. Rules and good habits aren't the enemy, but they were never meant to stand between a hurting person and the Lord. And when Jesus does something good, do what the crowd did, and rejoice "at all the glorious things He was doing" (Luke 13:17). I'd rather be in that crowd than the one hitting reply-all, and I say that as a stamper who once got stuck in a drawer.
